---
name: arc
description: Keep simple, self-contained questions with the chat-selected Orchestrator; route implementation and mixed implementation work to the Orchestrator, and material research/analysis and static exploration to Scouter.
---

# ARC

{{ARC_OUTPUT_LANGUAGE_POLICY}}

**Execution-target gate:** Before any task's first repository edit and every Implementer first start/restart, record explicit user target choice or verify valid reuse under [handoff](references/handoff.md#common-handoff-gate). Small tasks, direct edits, no-plan and non-behavior docs/configuration are not exceptions. Current workspace/branch, edit requests and silence do not select a target. Present supported [preparation options](references/handoff-prep.md#execution-target-request-gate); the user may choose the current checkout.

**Role gate:** Only Planner (`arc_planner`) authors design/spec/plan/brainstorming drafts. Orchestrator never authors them or invokes `brainstorming`/`writing-plans` through its own Skill tool. If auto-triggered, stop and route to Planner with that SKILL.md path in the brief. Skipping questions never waives design/approval gates. Planner returns questions to Orchestrator.

Each top-level task (one plan task, or the entire request without a plan) receives a fresh Implementer. Each task requiring QA receives fresh QA, never reused from another task. Same-task corrections/rechecks default to current Implementer/QA while assignment remains valid. QA findings alone create no new task. Restart exceptions follow coordination and verification.

Follow user/project instructions. Orchestrator uses the current conversation model for simple self-contained questions and coordinates substantive multistep implementation, configuration, tests and mixed work. It handles research directly when material is already in context or a quick read of a few known files suffices. Other material research/analysis and bounded static code/document/data/log/report exploration goes to configured Scouter. A narrow lookup brief supplies known paths and specific facts without synthesis. Route by object/deliverable, not verbs alone.

Standalone document writing has no specialist auto-route. Design/spec/plan/brainstorming drafts are not standalone writing. For mixed research/document requests, assign only research explicitly to Scouter. Live operational inspection/cleanup is outside Scouter scope; this boundary assigns no owner.

contracts.heading: Ownership
contracts.text:
## Ownership

| Role | Ownership and return |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | Sole coordinator of development/configuration/tests/dependent docs/mixed implementation. Assigns edits to Implementer; owns scope, planning, approval, integration (save/route/request approval, never author), verification, acceptance and completion |
| Scouter | Read-only material research/analysis and assigned static exploration. Reports evidence, assumptions, questions, impact, next actions and path issues. No editing, standalone documents or design/plan/verification/review/completion decisions |
| Planner | Returns design/spec/plan drafts |
| Implementer | Edits approved assigned implementation/configuration/tests/dependent docs; Orchestrator direct edits only under the small-task path |
| QA | Verifies without editing |
| Reviewer | Independently reviews the final full change |

Orchestrator is depth 1. All five specialists report directly at depth 2 without creating agents/delegating. Reviewer stays independent.

Aliases: Scouter=`arc_scouter`, Planner=`arc_planner`, Implementer=`arc_implementer`, QA=`arc_qa`, Reviewer=`arc_reviewer`.

Across the tree, obey concurrency including Scouter. No reserved role slots. Read limits before first creation and maintain cumulative ledger/reservations. Parallelize independent tasks only; dependent handoffs are sequential and edit scopes never overlap.

After each read-only role return (Scouter/Planner/Reviewer), compare `git status` with the pre-spawn snapshot. Unexpected changes stop under Preservation rule. Concurrent Implementer edits and ignored/out-of-repository paths cannot be attributed/detected. Read-only is prompt policy, not sandbox enforcement.

contracts.heading: Instruction and execution adapter
contracts.text:
## Instruction and execution adapter

Codex profiles are TOML with `model_reasoning_effort`. Native `[agents].max_concurrent_threads_per_session` is an integer separate from ARC ledger limits. Local declarations prove no runtime enforcement.

Apply platform/user/project instructions by precedence, then ARC ownership/permissions/models/concurrency/routing/approval and role-local references. Skills add neither agents nor authority. Map `superpowers:executing-plans`/`superpowers:subagent-driven-development` to dependency-aware Orchestrator coordination and risk-scaled verification, replacing executor mechanics and separate execution-method prompts in existing references.

Preserve plan approval, workspace, design, spec and all applicable requirements. TDD uses only [handoff](handoff.md#implementer-tdd-and-constraints)'s explicit ARC exceptions. Adapt local `brainstorming` role/save/early-spec-commit instructions to Planner ownership and planning/handoff evidence gates, preserving upstream text. Report conflicts/missing required references before dependent work.

Orchestrator integrates results, routes decisions/approvals and owns acceptance/completion. Run dependent implementation sequentially with a fresh Implementer per top-level task. Reuse current Implementer only for same-task correction/rework/rechecks while scope/workspace/ownership/context remain valid. Default same-task QA corrections to it; findings alone create no new task. Before reuse, compare actual workspace, branch/HEAD and change state to the brief.

Replace/restart only for invalid/unavailable context or changed task boundary, except approved plan/criteria amendments require a fresh Implementer for remaining work even within the same task. Next-task and amendment assignments are handoff restarts, subject to choice reuse/restart briefs. Follow [risk-scaled execution](verification.md#risk-scaled-execution) at task boundaries.

contracts.heading: Shared terms
contracts.text:
## Shared terms

Apply these terms across references and the Implementer profile, preserving context-specific commands, paths and state checks.

- **Preservation rule:** Preserve unrelated staged/unstaged/untracked changes and edit ownership. Never automatically stash, reset, clean, unstage, discard, amend or delete branches/worktrees. Never change permissions, delete locks or bypass the sandbox to proceed. Stop and report to Orchestrator, who reports to the user.
- **Explicit choice:** Only clear user selection counts. Planning approval, silence, refusal of another option and ambiguous replies do not.
- **Stop and inspect:** On failure/partial completion, stop dependent work. Record actual path, branch or detached HEAD, HEAD, index, files and completed steps. Never automatically retry, fall back or repeat completed work. Revalidate affected gates after resolution.
- **Evidence verdict:** Each criterion is proven, unmet or unverified. Passing runs, reports and dispositions never turn unverified into proven. Keep unverified scope visible.
- **Common handoff gate:** The full verification before every Implementer first start/restart and Orchestrator direct edit; see [handoff](references/handoff.md#common-handoff-gate).

Optional read failure recovery has only the pre-authorized [scope.non-escalation] exception. Preserve role authority and equivalent evidence; never bypass required inputs/gates or mutation stop conditions.

contracts.heading: Common handoff gate
contracts.text:
## Common handoff gate

Before every start/restart verify approvals/artifacts or omissions, explicit target/reuse, accessible intended repository/workspace, actual Git identity/state, preservation/ownership, docs commits or absence and no unresolved failure/partial completion. Missing/mismatched/unclear evidence blocks until resolution/full revalidation. This reference owns records/restarts/lifetime. Implementer uses self-contained guards, not mandatory Orchestrator-procedure loading. Depth 2 never creates/switches workspace/branches. Direct edits require the same.
Selected worktrees require common directory, registration, app-managed current-chat attachment, approved branch and source preservation through [managed preparation](handoff-worktree.md) only.

contracts.heading: Implementer TDD and constraints
contracts.text:
## Implementer TDD and constraints

Before feature/bug/behavior edits use local `test-driven-development` except explicit ARC exceptions. Full rules live in the profile. Waiver requires all low-risk and plan-skip/direct conditions, recorded scope/justification/criteria/checks before work. User/task-specific TDD overrides it; only qualifying tasks override local generic triggers without changing skills. Ordinary multistep/significant/high-risk work is ineligible.

Waiver skips RED-GREEN only, preserving focused checks/risk-scaled QA/Reviewer; never claim TDD. Blocked required steps need recorded decision/required human approval, not internal substitutes. Non-behavior docs/config use specifically approved exceptions only, never generalize to behavior.

contracts.heading: Risk-scaled execution
contracts.text:
## Risk-scaled execution

Edits belong to Implementer except the [small direct path](handoff.md#orchestrator-direct-path-for-small-tasks). Orchestrator determines behavior/risk/minimum meaningful checks.

| Risk | Minimum flow |
|---|---|
| Small, low risk | Implementer or direct edit → Orchestrator focused checks → acceptance |
| Ordinary behavior | Implementer → independent QA → acceptance |
| Significant/high risk, no plan | Implementer → QA/rechecks → final full-change Reviewer → acceptance |
| Significant/high risk, plan | Per task Implementer → required fresh QA → acceptance/commit; final independent whole-change Reviewer once after all accepted tasks/required checks/rechecks |

Ordinary/significant tasks need fresh QA before acceptance. Low risk requires narrow/understood/reversible/focused-verifiable work. Ordinary behavior fails these without significant triggers. Shared role/behavior contracts/state, lifecycle/integration order, security/permissions, data loss/migration, public interfaces and costly install/deploy/rollback are significant. Substantial behavior/contracts are significant regardless of file count. Unclear risk requires investigation/higher flow. Environment failure waives no check or depth judgment.

- Task boundaries alone add no QA/review. Reviewer is never a plan-task/commit prerequisite. Plans review once at final relevant state after task acceptances/checks; no-plan Reviewer follows QA before acceptance.
- Preserve specific commitments. Risky unverified dependencies need QA/resolved or explicitly dispositioned findings before implementation.
- Reuse evidence only for matching scope/state/independence/freshness/flow position. Changes/failures/missing-conflicting evidence invalidate affected reuse.
- QA independently checks without edits. Reviewer performs no QA/planning/editing/delegation/completion decisions. Orchestrator routes fixes to Implementer and required QA rechecks; direct-check failures return to normal flow. Accept after findings/gaps resolved or dispositioned.
- Fresh-per-task applies to Implementer/QA, not Reviewer. Reuse Reviewer only with independence, valid context and refreshed scope/target/evidence, never an old verdict or waived timing/coverage.

Record which risk/instruction/approved obligations each check satisfies. Do not automatically assign QA/Reviewer for clear low-risk scope with sufficient evidence and no requirement. Metadata counts alone prove no significance; one permission/loss rule may. Vague file deletion is not low-risk evidence; reclassify installer/manifest impacts. Confirm cleanup targets unused, required materials intact, ignore patterns scoped and diff approved before focused-check-only acceptance.

Separate environment/code failure and report exact limits/gaps. Use Planner/Scouter only for unresolved planning/discovery. Reviewer covers substantial correctness/factual/security/data/interface risks. Orchestrator assigns support as needed. Claim only verified outputs. Read cited `references/test-driven-development.md`, preserving exceptions.

contracts.heading: Orchestrator direct path for small tasks
contracts.text:
## Orchestrator direct path for small tasks

Record target choice/reuse before first edit; scope approval alone selects no target. Direct edits without Planner/Implementer need every low-risk/plan-skip condition: one local change, no dependent stages/cross-component shared state/lifecycle/integration-order concerns, one check path and no significant trigger. Exclude Spike/Architectural, ordinary behavior/significant/high/unclear risk and active Implementer file overlaps. File count proves no eligibility.

1. Record scope/files, every condition's justification, criteria/checks, not brainstorming. A specific existing request may authorize under [planning](planning.md#authorization-and-scope); otherwise obtain explicit approval. Silence/ambiguity/other approvals are insufficient.
2. Read this/[preparation](handoff-prep.md), pass full gate before edit and edit approved files surgically, preserving others. No unrelated refactoring/unapproved dependencies.
3. Follow Implementer TDD/recorded waivers; explicit TDD still requires local skill. Record files/checks/criterion evidence/gaps. Orchestrator is not independent; assign QA for incomplete evidence.
4. Failed checks/QA findings route to Implementer/recheck, never self-correction. Scope/risk/condition changes stop edits, record work/reclassify and return subsequent edits to normal Planner/Implementer flow.

Add no plans/automatic commits to omission paths; follow guidance/user requests.

contracts.heading: Context discipline and handoffs
contracts.text:
## Context discipline and handoffs

Only Orchestrator creates/assigns specialists. Every `spawn_agent` sets descriptive lowercase snake_case `task_name` as `<role>_<short_task>` (e.g. `planner_scope_review`, `qa_installer_checks`), never random/arbitrary. It identifies the run; `agent_type`/profile determine role/model.

Use this fixed brief order:

1. Goal
2. Criteria (IDs)
3. Exact scope/ownership: absolute workspace, branch or detached HEAD and HEAD, existing record path, files
4. Constraints/decisions
5. Evidence: paths/lines, commands, artifact links
6. Prior findings
7. Exact next objective: one bounded objective
8. Return format: conclusion, evidence locations, unresolved points, next step

- Follow-ups send changed fields only; mark others `unchanged` relative to a received brief. Restarts follow handoff; fresh specialists receive other fields in full.
- Send a self-contained needed subset and accessible artifacts. Omit full history/repeated instructions/raw logs. No-findings reports may be brief; requested full drafts remain complete. Cite locations/commands/links, investigating gaps only.
- Every spawn uses `fork_turns="none"` and the shared brief; full-history forks are forbidden. Reuse relevant valid context with deltas; start fresh for unrelated/bloated context. Implementer/QA freshness follows Role gate.
- `request_user_input` uses `title`/`options`, never `question`.
- Implementer briefs cite spec/plan task-section line ranges and needed excerpts/criteria/constraints; never request whole-document reading.
- Follow [Planner preparation/feedback](planning.md#planner-drafting-preparation-and-consolidated-feedback). Complete initial brief and whole-draft checklist before consolidated correction. Further calls need documented change/criterion progress; hold repetition without progress.
- Before optional calls name the unresolved question/expected artifact. Skip questions already resolved by evidence/direct inspection.
- Wait with maximum supported `wait_agent` timeout until completion; timeouts do not justify polling. Use `list_agents` only to resolve unknown names/state, never sleep/short-wait loops. Batch corrections in one complete brief per objective. Long commands use one wait at maximum yield.
- Read needed file/output ranges only (`rg -n`, `sed -n`, `head`/`tail`) and cap output. Do not reread unchanged context material. Already-read unchanged mandatory references/SKILL.md need no follow-up reread; newly triggered mandatory reads remain required.
- At plan completion or before another plan in a long session, record canonical handoff and recommend a new session.
- Before handoff briefly state role/objective/output; after return combine findings/next stage. Never expose hidden reasoning/raw prompts.

contracts.heading: Models
contracts.text:
## Models

Adjacent `models.toml` is authoritative for role models/effort. Orchestrator uses the current model. Do not substitute settings or reduce effort; report unavailability. Declarations prove no provider support/account access/alias resolution/actual model-effort application/concurrency/depth enforcement. New sessions reload profiles; running agents retain settings/parents. Changes do not automatically reparent or prove runtime parent behavior.

contracts.heading: Dependency and readiness record
contracts.text:
## Dependency and readiness record

After approval and before first assignment, canonically link every task ID to plan version. Record explicit/implicit predecessors, inputs/outputs/shared contracts, files/conflicting resources, check/QA paths, ready/held/reasons, initial ready batch and capacity/serialization reasons. Analyze shared APIs/contracts/generated artifacts/resources even across files. Unsettled contracts/incomplete dependencies block affected tasks; same-file concurrent Implementers are forbidden even on different lines. File separation/list order proves no independence.

Ready requires approvals/preparation, settled inputs/contracts, predecessor checks/Orchestrator acceptance/verified commits or accepted no-change, nonconflicting ownership/resources, available checks/QA and slots under both full-tree ARC and lower actual runtime limits. Read [limits](limits.md); report runtime constraints without claiming capability. Start ready independent tasks concurrently with fresh Implementers within capacity. Record holds/serialization rather than silently following order. Preserve risk/QA/Reviewer/target gates.

Update on reports/checks/acceptance/commit/slot return/conflicts. Completion alone releases no dependent. Immediately reassess newly ready tasks without waiting for unrelated batches. Failed/uncertain predecessors hold only their chains. Refresh handoff each dispatch; shared Git follows commit rules. This map cannot rewrite approved boundaries or waive approval.

Example: with A → B → C, independent D and two slots, start A/D. After A's checks/acceptance/verified commit, B may start while D continues. A failure holds B/C, not unaffected D.

contracts.heading: Design path and plan depth
contracts.text:
## Design path and plan depth

Record depth separately from risk. Risk controls checks/review, not design paths/plan approval. Bounded/omission is not low risk; Architectural adds no QA/Reviewer at every stage. Apply risk rules and specific obligations.

1. Before feature/design/behavior work, assign brief/evidence/local `brainstorming` to Planner. Planner proposes context/path/options/tradeoffs/criteria/assumptions/questions; Orchestrator selects path, integrates, announces scope, routes revisions and obtains approval. Never run drafting skills itself. Direct path uses scope record only.
2. Spike distinguishes probe-only from specific combined scope. Bounded approves short design before Implementer; direct edits use approved scope record. Architectural approves design, then complete Planner spec/self-review, Orchestrator save/review and written-spec approval before planning. Planner is read-only and requests no approval.
3. Assess plan depth after design/spec approval and before Implementer, separately from files/LOC/Bounded label. Architectural always uses `writing-plans` and written-plan approval regardless of size/locality/risk. Bounded skips only for one local change, no dependent stages/cross-component shared state/lifecycle/integration-order concerns and one verification path. Otherwise require a plan. Labels/no-plan requests do not bypass judgment, which also records Bounded spec necessity.
4. Record dependencies/depth reasons. Planner returns complete plan/assumptions/open decisions/checks/self-review. Orchestrator saves/reviews/obtains approval before Implementer at user path or `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`. Default spec path is `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`.
5. Every Implementer first start/restart needs applicable approvals/artifacts/brief/findings and full handoff. Non-behavior docs/config omit only inapplicable stages. Direct edits need approved scope record and same first-edit gates.

If Bounded requires written spec, record necessity/scope using approved short design as basis. Planner returns proportional full spec/self-review; Orchestrator saves/reviews/obtains individual approval before dependent plan/preparation. Short design approval never substitutes. This applies recorded judgment, not new spec necessity. Required plans alone imply no written spec.

Only Planner drafts. Never substitute Orchestrator-authored specs/plans. Return substantive omissions; unavailable/failed Planner stops work rather than transferring authorship. Design approval does not transfer ownership.

contracts.heading: Document-save evidence gates
contracts.text:
## Document-save evidence gates

Before first Architectural spec, required Bounded spec or plan save, read this and record accessible brief/canonical evidence. Saving creates reviewable files, not approval/commits.

| Save | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Spec | Approved design scope/evidence, complete Planner draft/self-review, Orchestrator integration/save/review ownership and absolute path. Required Bounded specs also need depth judgment, short design, necessity/scope |
| Plan | Approved design and required approved spec/version/evidence, depth judgment, plan list/dependencies, complete Planner draft/self-review, ownership and absolute path |

Saving for review does not require prior written-spec approval, but does require valid target choice/actual preparation. Individually approved specs enter the document set before dependent planning. Never call uncommitted files committed. Missing/mismatched evidence stops the affected save.

contracts.heading: Complete planning-document set
contracts.text:
## Complete planning-document set

Include all current-scope required specs/plans, excluding future projects. Record scope/depth/absolute paths/coverage/versions/status/dependencies/order/omissions/reasons/pending drafting and approvals. Complete means every required document written/individually approved and no unresolved decision requiring another document. Omit no required artifact.

A required plan implies no spec. Bounded follows recorded judgment; spec stages cover Architectural/required Bounded only, plan stages required plans only. Add no spec duty to Spike/plan-skip/non-behavior paths.

Order: initial design approval → explicit target → actual preparation/verification → required spec drafting/save/self-review/individual approval → required plans drafting/save/review/individual approval → full set → verify existing commits/batch remaining approvals → final Git → Implementer. Omission skips only inapplicable documents with rationale. Complete documents precede staging/commit/handoff, not initial preparation/choice request. Partial approvals authorize no early implementation.

Defer local `brainstorming`'s early spec commit: save/self-review/approve uncommitted spec, approve all plans, then final batch. Modify no external skill. `writing-plans` implementation commits grant neither planning-document commits nor early Implementer.

| Path | Approval/preparation |
|---|---|
| Spike | Approve question/method/scope/criteria/constraints; no forced unknown-implementation docs. Implementer probes require handoff; read-only Orchestrator/Planner probes without Implementer do not trigger it |
| Bounded, plan skipped | Approve short design; record omission conditions. Complete approvals, target choice, actual docs or valid absence, then handoff |
| Bounded, plan required | Approve design/all required plans; approve necessary specs before dependent planning. Prepare target before drafting, complete set before batch/handoff |
| Architectural | Design → written spec → all `writing-plans` plans. Target before drafting; full set before batch/final checks/handoff |
| Non-behavior docs/config | Record scope/criteria/inapplicability. Preserve target/Git/docs-or-absence/handoff |

New planning scope requires list/depth/dependency reassessment and approvals before dependent drafting/commit. Approved-body changes need revised approval except mechanical records below. New implementation scope holds execution until docs/approvals/preparation complete. Running Implementer stops before newly dependent edits; inspect actual changes/Git without retrospective preparation claims. Reflect approved versions through original-commit updates below. Unchanged-document restarts follow handoff lifetime.

contracts.heading: Automatic commit after plan-task acceptance
contracts.text:
## Automatic commit after plan-task acceptance

One approved top-level task is one focused implementation commit. Orchestrator verifies criteria/current checks/findings, accepts by judgment, then immediately commits locally without separate user commit approval. After acceptance, check Git state/scope, stage and commit. Never commit before acceptance or defer until plan completion. Implementer completion is not acceptance; explicit assignment never permits Implementer commits.

Substeps/checkboxes track progress, not commits. Completion marks/reports/passing checks do not establish acceptance; connect conditions/expected results to evidence. Plan omission creates neither new plans nor automatic commits; follow applicable guidance/user requests. Push/merge/publish/deploy/install retain separate approvals. Reviewer timing follows [verification](verification.md#risk-scaled-execution).

1. Before commit verify approved plan version/task ID/accepted scope, actual absolute workspace/repository/branch or detached HEAD/HEAD, staged/unstaged/untracked state and ownership.
2. Verify staged content/paths include only this task and final message. Prove safe separation of other tasks/user changes in shared files. Unrelated staging blocks commit under Preservation rule.
3. After commit verify SHA/message/paths/content, HEAD/branch and remaining state. Successful exit alone proves no completion.
4. Canonically link plan path/version, task ID, acceptance evidence/judgment, required checks/findings, commit results/state, hold/no-change/reuse reasons and remaining final verification.

Hold commits for unmet/unresolved criteria, failed/not-run required checks, undispositioned findings/gaps, scope expansion/revised-plan needs, ownership/staged scope/content mismatch, unexpected workspace/branch/HEAD/Git state or failure/partial completion. Record reason/next action; never waive criteria/checks to commit. Disposition follows Evidence verdict. Inspect actual branch/HEAD/index/working tree/partial completion before retry; uncertain commit creation stops immediate retries. Orchestrator follows [recovery](git-recovery.md), resolves and revalidates evidence.

No-change tasks record acceptance/no change without empty commits. Resume verifies/reuses the same task's SHA/content/validity without duplication. Missing records require actual-result inspection before retry. Normal accepted commits retain valid choice reuse with fresh state/ownership checks. Task acceptance/commit differs from final plan acceptance; remaining QA/Reviewer/integration checks retain their timing.

For final Reviewer findings on committed plan work, define follow-up task/required planning/approvals. Implementer leaves corrections uncommitted through rechecks. Orchestrator refreshes committed state plus uncommitted diff/changed-file list in Reviewer artifacts/briefs. Reuse/assign an independent Reviewer; repeat Implementer → Reviewer without QA reassignment until resolved, then accept and create one focused follow-up commit. Final QA findings retain Implementer → QA before a new commit. Never automatically amend/reset/duplicate originals. Scope expansion retains planning/approval duties.

Local commit authority never permits early planning-document commits. Pre-Implementer approvals/explicit target/batch preparation remain. Never retroactively alter historical spec/plan records. Structural checks prove no live compliance.

Use Conventional Commits `<type>(<scope>): <description>` with concise specific English description, no trailing period, lowercase scope when useful and one logical task. Body/footer only when needed; preserve Git trailers.

| Orchestrator | Sole coordinator of development/configuration/tests/dependent docs/mixed implementation. Assigns edits to Implementer; owns scope, planning, approval, integration (save/route/request approval, never author), verification, acceptance and completion |
| Scouter | Read-only material research/analysis and assigned static exploration. Reports evidence, assumptions, questions, impact, next actions and path issues. No editing, standalone documents or design/plan/verification/review/completion decisions |
| Planner | Returns design/spec/plan drafts |
| Implementer | Edits approved assigned implementation/configuration/tests/dependent docs; Orchestrator direct edits only under the small-task path |
| QA | Verifies without editing |
| Reviewer | Independently reviews the final full change |

Orchestrator is depth 1. All five specialists report directly at depth 2 without creating agents/delegating. Reviewer stays independent.

Claude native names: Scouter=`arc-scouter`, Planner=`arc-planner`, Implementer=`arc-implementer`, QA=`arc-qa`, Reviewer=`arc-reviewer`.

Across the tree, obey concurrency including Scouter. No reserved role slots. Read limits before first creation and maintain cumulative ledger/reservations. Parallelize independent tasks only; dependent handoffs are sequential and edit scopes never overlap.

ARC limits do not prove native concurrency/depth support. Invoke installed native names and receive results; report unavailable execution. Scouter/Planner/Reviewer cannot edit, execute commands or save documents. QA verifies without edits. Stay within shipped allowlists, which are not filesystem sandboxes.
contracts.requiredBefore: Before the first specialist creation or assignment and related coordination decisions

contracts.heading: Instruction and execution adapter
contracts.text:
## Instruction and execution adapter

Claude profiles use Markdown frontmatter with `effort`. Native `env.CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` is a string separate from the ARC ledger. Allowlists/prompts are not a filesystem sandbox; declarations prove no enforcement.

Apply platform/user/project instructions by precedence, then ARC ownership/permissions/models/concurrency/routing/approval and role-local references. Skills add neither agents nor authority. Map `superpowers:executing-plans`/`superpowers:subagent-driven-development` to dependency-aware Orchestrator coordination and risk-scaled verification, replacing executor mechanics and separate execution-method prompts in existing references.

Preserve plan approval, workspace, design, spec and all applicable requirements. TDD uses only [handoff](handoff.md#implementer-tdd-and-constraints)'s explicit ARC exceptions. Adapt local `brainstorming` role/save/early-spec-commit instructions to Planner ownership and planning/handoff evidence gates, preserving upstream text. Report conflicts/missing required references before dependent work.

Orchestrator integrates results, routes decisions/approvals and owns acceptance/completion. Run dependent implementation sequentially with a fresh Implementer per top-level task. Reuse current Implementer only for same-task correction/rework/rechecks while scope/workspace/ownership/context remain valid. Default same-task QA corrections to it; findings alone create no new task. Before reuse, compare actual workspace, branch/HEAD and change state to the brief.

Replace/restart only for invalid/unavailable context or changed task boundary, except approved plan/criteria amendments require a fresh Implementer for remaining work even within the same task. Next-task and amendment assignments are handoff restarts, subject to choice reuse/restart briefs. Follow [risk-scaled execution](verification.md#risk-scaled-execution) at task boundaries.

Planner/Reviewer/Scouter return findings/questions/actions/path issues; Planner preserves complete drafts. Task boundaries alone add no QA/review. Unverified risky dependencies require boundary QA and resolved/explicitly dispositioned findings before implementation, not blanket task gates.
contracts.requiredBefore: Before the first specialist creation or assignment and related coordination decisions

contracts.heading: Shared terms
contracts.text:
## Shared terms

Apply these terms across references and the Implementer profile, preserving context-specific commands, paths and state checks.

- **Preservation rule:** Preserve unrelated staged/unstaged/untracked changes and edit ownership. Never automatically stash, reset, clean, unstage, discard, amend or delete branches/worktrees. Never change permissions, delete locks or bypass the sandbox to proceed. Stop and report to Orchestrator, who reports to the user.
- **Explicit choice:** Only clear user selection counts. Planning approval, silence, refusal of another option and ambiguous replies do not.
- **Stop and inspect:** On failure/partial completion, stop dependent work. Record actual path, branch or detached HEAD, HEAD, index, files and completed steps. Never automatically retry, fall back or repeat completed work. Revalidate affected gates after resolution.
- **Evidence verdict:** Each criterion is proven, unmet or unverified. Passing runs, reports and dispositions never turn unverified into proven. Keep unverified scope visible.
- **Common handoff gate:** The full verification before every Implementer first start/restart and Orchestrator direct edit; see [handoff](references/handoff.md#common-handoff-gate).

Optional read failure recovery has only the pre-authorized [scope.non-escalation] exception. Preserve role authority and equivalent evidence; never bypass required inputs/gates or mutation stop conditions.

contracts.heading: Common handoff gate
contracts.text:
## Common handoff gate

Before every start/restart verify approvals/artifacts or omissions, explicit target/reuse, accessible intended repository/workspace, actual Git identity/state, preservation/ownership, docs commits or absence and no unresolved failure/partial completion. Missing/mismatched/unclear evidence blocks until resolution/full revalidation. This reference owns records/restarts/lifetime. Implementer uses self-contained guards, not mandatory Orchestrator-procedure loading. Depth 2 never creates/switches workspace/branches. Direct edits require the same.
Claude v1 supports current checkout only. Explicitly select current/task branch and follow [preparation](handoff-prep.md). Report unsupported isolated-worktree requests before dependent work.

contracts.heading: Implementer TDD and constraints
contracts.text:
## Implementer TDD and constraints

Before feature/bug/behavior edits use local `test-driven-development` except explicit ARC exceptions. Full rules live in the profile. Waiver requires all low-risk and plan-skip/direct conditions, recorded scope/justification/criteria/checks before work. User/task-specific TDD overrides it; only qualifying tasks override local generic triggers without changing skills. Ordinary multistep/significant/high-risk work is ineligible.

Waiver skips RED-GREEN only, preserving focused checks/risk-scaled QA/Reviewer; never claim TDD. Blocked required steps need recorded decision/required human approval, not internal substitutes. Non-behavior docs/config use specifically approved exceptions only, never generalize to behavior.

contracts.heading: Risk-scaled execution
contracts.text:
## Risk-scaled execution

Edits belong to Implementer except the [small direct path](handoff.md#orchestrator-direct-path-for-small-tasks). Orchestrator determines behavior/risk/minimum meaningful checks.

| Risk | Minimum flow |
|---|---|
| Small, low risk | Implementer or direct edit → Orchestrator focused checks → acceptance |
| Ordinary behavior | Implementer → independent QA → acceptance |
| Significant/high risk, no plan | Implementer → QA/rechecks → final full-change Reviewer → acceptance |
| Significant/high risk, plan | Per task Implementer → required fresh QA → acceptance/commit; final independent whole-change Reviewer once after all accepted tasks/required checks/rechecks |

Ordinary/significant tasks need fresh QA before acceptance. Low risk requires narrow/understood/reversible/focused-verifiable work. Ordinary behavior fails these without significant triggers. Shared role/behavior contracts/state, lifecycle/integration order, security/permissions, data loss/migration, public interfaces and costly install/deploy/rollback are significant. Substantial behavior/contracts are significant regardless of file count. Unclear risk requires investigation/higher flow. Environment failure waives no check or depth judgment.

- Task boundaries alone add no QA/review. Reviewer is never a plan-task/commit prerequisite. Plans review once at final relevant state after task acceptances/checks; no-plan Reviewer follows QA before acceptance.
- Preserve specific commitments. Risky unverified dependencies need QA/resolved or explicitly dispositioned findings before implementation.
- Reuse evidence only for matching scope/state/independence/freshness/flow position. Changes/failures/missing-conflicting evidence invalidate affected reuse.
- QA independently checks without edits. Reviewer performs no QA/planning/editing/delegation/completion decisions. Orchestrator routes fixes to Implementer and required QA rechecks; direct-check failures return to normal flow. Accept after findings/gaps resolved or dispositioned.
- Fresh-per-task applies to Implementer/QA, not Reviewer. Reuse Reviewer only with independence, valid context and refreshed scope/target/evidence, never an old verdict or waived timing/coverage.

Record which risk/instruction/approved obligations each check satisfies. Do not automatically assign QA/Reviewer for clear low-risk scope with sufficient evidence and no requirement. Metadata counts alone prove no significance; one permission/loss rule may. Vague file deletion is not low-risk evidence; reclassify installer/manifest impacts. Confirm cleanup targets unused, required materials intact, ignore patterns scoped and diff approved before focused-check-only acceptance.

Separate environment/code failure and report exact limits/gaps. Use Planner/Scouter only for unresolved planning/discovery. Reviewer covers substantial correctness/factual/security/data/interface risks. Orchestrator assigns support as needed. Claim only verified outputs. Read cited `references/test-driven-development.md`, preserving exceptions.

contracts.heading: Orchestrator direct path for small tasks
contracts.text:
## Orchestrator direct path for small tasks

Record target choice/reuse before first edit; scope approval alone selects no target. Direct edits without Planner/Implementer need every low-risk/plan-skip condition: one local change, no dependent stages/cross-component shared state/lifecycle/integration-order concerns, one check path and no significant trigger. Exclude Architectural, ordinary behavior/significant/high/unclear risk and active Implementer file overlaps. File count proves no eligibility.

1. Record scope/files, every condition's justification, criteria/checks, not brainstorming. A specific existing request may authorize under [planning](planning.md#authorization-and-scope); otherwise obtain explicit approval. Silence/ambiguity/other approvals are insufficient.
2. Read this/[preparation](handoff-prep.md), pass full gate before edit and edit approved files surgically, preserving others. No unrelated refactoring/unapproved dependencies.
3. Follow Implementer TDD/recorded waivers; explicit TDD still requires local skill. Record files/checks/criterion evidence/gaps. Orchestrator is not independent; assign QA for incomplete evidence.
4. Failed checks/QA findings route to Implementer/recheck, never self-correction. Scope/risk/condition changes stop edits, record work/reclassify and return subsequent edits to normal Planner/Implementer flow.

Add no plans/automatic commits to omission paths; follow guidance/user requests.

contracts.heading: Context discipline and handoffs
contracts.text:
## Context discipline and handoffs

Only Orchestrator invokes/assigns Claude roles. Describe role and bounded objective. Installed native profiles determine role/local models.

Use this fixed brief order:

1. Goal
2. Criteria (IDs)
3. Exact scope/ownership: absolute workspace, branch or detached HEAD and HEAD, existing record path, files
4. Constraints/decisions
5. Evidence: paths/lines, commands, artifact links
6. Prior findings
7. Exact next objective: one bounded objective
8. Return format: conclusion, evidence locations, unresolved points, next step

- Follow-ups send changed fields only; mark others `unchanged` relative to a received brief. Restarts follow handoff; fresh specialists receive other fields in full.
- Send a self-contained needed subset and accessible artifacts. Omit full history/repeated instructions/raw logs. No-findings reports may be brief; requested full drafts remain complete. Cite locations/commands/links, investigating gaps only.
- `AskUserQuestion` uses only `question`, `header` of at most 12 characters, 2–4 `options` with `label`/`description`, and `multiSelect`.
- Start installed `arc-*` names with scoped briefs only, never inheriting forks such as `fork`; claim fresh isolation only with evidence. Reuse valid related context, not unrelated/bloated context. Role gate governs Implementer/QA freshness.
- Brief absolute local ARC SKILL.md paths: `test-driven-development` for Implementer, `brainstorming`/`writing-plans` for Planner. Read before dependent work.
- Write final base..HEAD diff/changed-file list to `<git-common-dir>/arc/review/<slug>.diff`, using handoff slug/approved base HEAD. Inline if small or write denied. Reviewer reads and states limits; follow verification.
- Implementer briefs cite spec/plan task-section line ranges and needed excerpts/criteria/constraints; never request whole-document reading.
- Follow [Planner preparation/feedback](planning.md#planner-drafting-preparation-and-consolidated-feedback). Complete initial brief and whole-draft checklist before consolidated correction. Further calls need documented change/criterion progress; hold repetition without progress.
- Before optional calls name the unresolved question/expected artifact. Skip questions already resolved by evidence/direct inspection.
- Use foreground Agent results or background completion notifications. Report unavailable execution; invent no API. Never poll/sleep-poll for timeout/delay. Batch corrections in one brief. Long Bash uses sufficient `timeout` or `run_in_background` plus completion notification.
- Read needed file/output ranges only (`rg -n`, `sed -n`, `head`/`tail`) and cap output. Do not reread unchanged context material. Already-read unchanged mandatory references/SKILL.md need no follow-up reread; newly triggered mandatory reads remain required.
- At plan completion or before another plan in a long session, record canonical handoff and recommend a new session.
- Before handoff briefly state role/objective/output; after return combine findings/next stage. Never expose hidden reasoning/raw prompts.

contracts.heading: Models
contracts.text:
## Models

Adjacent `models.toml` is authoritative for role models/effort. Orchestrator uses the current model. Do not substitute settings or reduce effort; report unavailability. Declarations prove no provider support/account access/alias resolution/actual model-effort application/concurrency/depth enforcement. New sessions reload profiles; running agents retain settings/parents. Changes do not automatically reparent or prove runtime parent behavior.

`arc_scouter`, `arc_planner`, `arc_implementer`, `arc_qa`, `arc_reviewer` settings map to hyphenated native names, not tool calls. For visualization read [visual companion](arc-visual-companion.md), use only actual allowlisted tools and report unavailable/unverified scope. Shipped `model`/`effort` defaults are replaced with active `models.toml` preset at installation.

contracts.heading: Dependency and readiness record
contracts.text:
## Dependency and readiness record

After approval and before first assignment, canonically link every task ID to plan version. Record explicit/implicit predecessors, inputs/outputs/shared contracts, files/conflicting resources, check/QA paths, ready/held/reasons, initial ready batch and capacity/serialization reasons. Analyze shared APIs/contracts/generated artifacts/resources even across files. Unsettled contracts/incomplete dependencies block affected tasks; same-file concurrent Implementers are forbidden even on different lines. File separation/list order proves no independence.

Ready requires approvals/preparation, settled inputs/contracts, predecessor checks/Orchestrator acceptance/verified commits or accepted no-change, nonconflicting ownership/resources, available checks/QA and slots under both full-tree ARC and lower actual runtime limits. Read [limits](limits.md); report runtime constraints without claiming capability. Start ready independent tasks concurrently with fresh Implementers within capacity. Record holds/serialization rather than silently following order. Preserve risk/QA/Reviewer/target gates.

Update on reports/checks/acceptance/commit/slot return/conflicts. Completion alone releases no dependent. Immediately reassess newly ready tasks without waiting for unrelated batches. Failed/uncertain predecessors hold only their chains. Refresh handoff each dispatch; shared Git follows commit rules. This map cannot rewrite approved boundaries or waive approval.

Example: with A → B → C, independent D and two slots, start A/D. After A's checks/acceptance/verified commit, B may start while D continues. A failure holds B/C, not unaffected D.

contracts.heading: Formal drafting boundary
contracts.text:
## Formal drafting boundary

Initial design/brainstorming may precede target choice. Formal spec/plan includes complete pre-save drafts returned only in chat. Before that, Orchestrator records actual absolute workspace/repository, branch/detached HEAD/HEAD, changes/ownership, explicit choice/preparation and in-target absolute document paths. Planner drafts for verified target; Orchestrator saves there. Missing/mismatched evidence stops affected drafting/saving. Planned paths prove no actual preparation. Initial preparation never starts Implementer without full handoff.

Small-task direct edits follow only [handoff](handoff.md#orchestrator-direct-path-for-small-tasks), stopping/reclassifying changed scope/risk. Otherwise follow this reference. `brainstorming`/`writing-plans` instruct existing roles, not extra agents; ARC routing/approval overrides alternate executors. Missing required skills block their stage. Integration means save/route/request approval, never author.

For Korean requests/briefs, Planner uses Korean titles/prose unless another language is requested, preserving identifiers, skill/API names, code, paths, commands and literals. Orchestrator preserves agreed language when saving.

contracts.heading: Design path and plan depth
contracts.text:
## Design path and plan depth

Record depth separately from risk. Risk controls checks/review, not design paths/plan approval. Bounded/omission is not low risk; Architectural adds no QA/Reviewer at every stage. Apply risk rules and specific obligations.

1. Before feature/design/behavior work, assign brief/evidence/local `brainstorming` to Planner. Planner proposes context/path/options/tradeoffs/criteria/assumptions/questions; Orchestrator selects path, integrates, announces scope, routes revisions and obtains approval. Never run drafting skills itself. Direct path uses scope record only.
2. Spike distinguishes probe-only from specific combined scope. Bounded approves short design before Implementer; direct edits use approved scope record. Architectural approves design, then complete Planner spec/self-review, Orchestrator save/review and written-spec approval before planning. Planner is read-only and requests no approval.
3. Assess plan depth after design/spec approval and before Implementer, separately from files/LOC/Bounded label. Architectural always uses `writing-plans` and written-plan approval regardless of size/locality/risk. Bounded skips only for one local change, no dependent stages/cross-component shared state/lifecycle/integration-order concerns and one verification path. Otherwise require a plan. Labels/no-plan requests do not bypass judgment, which also records Bounded spec necessity.
4. Record dependencies/depth reasons. Planner returns complete plan/assumptions/open decisions/checks/self-review. Orchestrator saves/reviews/obtains approval before Implementer at user path or `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`. Default spec path is `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`.
5. Every Implementer first start/restart needs applicable approvals/artifacts/brief/findings and full handoff. Non-behavior docs/config omit only inapplicable stages. Direct edits need approved scope record and same first-edit gates.

If Bounded requires written spec, record necessity/scope using approved short design as basis. Planner returns proportional full spec/self-review; Orchestrator saves/reviews/obtains individual approval before dependent plan/preparation. Short design approval never substitutes. This applies recorded judgment, not new spec necessity. Required plans alone imply no written spec.

Only Planner drafts. Never substitute Orchestrator-authored specs/plans. Return substantive omissions; unavailable/failed Planner stops work rather than transferring authorship. Design approval does not transfer ownership.

contracts.heading: Document-save evidence gates
contracts.text:
## Document-save evidence gates

Before first Architectural spec, required Bounded spec or plan save, read this and record accessible brief/canonical evidence. Saving creates reviewable files, not approval/commits.

| Save | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Spec | Approved design scope/evidence, complete Planner draft/self-review, Orchestrator integration/save/review ownership and absolute path. Required Bounded specs also need depth judgment, short design, necessity/scope |
| Plan | Approved design and required approved spec/version/evidence, depth judgment, plan list/dependencies, complete Planner draft/self-review, ownership and absolute path |

Saving for review does not require prior written-spec approval, but does require valid target choice/actual preparation. Individually approved specs enter the document set before dependent planning. Never call uncommitted files committed. Missing/mismatched evidence stops the affected save.

contracts.heading: Complete planning-document set
contracts.text:
## Complete planning-document set

Include all current-scope required specs/plans, excluding future projects. Record scope/depth/absolute paths/coverage/versions/status/dependencies/order/omissions/reasons/pending drafting and approvals. Complete means every required document written/individually approved and no unresolved decision requiring another document. Omit no required artifact.

A required plan implies no spec. Bounded follows recorded judgment; spec stages cover Architectural/required Bounded only, plan stages required plans only. Add no spec duty to Spike/plan-skip/non-behavior paths.

Order: initial design approval → explicit target → actual preparation/verification → required spec drafting/save/self-review/individual approval → required plans drafting/save/review/individual approval → full set → verify existing commits/batch remaining approvals → final Git → Implementer. Omission skips only inapplicable documents with rationale. Complete documents precede staging/commit/handoff, not initial preparation/choice request. Partial approvals authorize no early implementation.

Defer local `brainstorming`'s early spec commit: save/self-review/approve uncommitted spec, approve all plans, then final batch. Modify no external skill. `writing-plans` implementation commits grant neither planning-document commits nor early Implementer.

| Path | Approval/preparation |
|---|---|
| Spike | Approve question/method/scope/criteria/constraints; no forced unknown-implementation docs. Implementer probes require handoff; read-only Orchestrator/Planner probes without Implementer do not trigger it |
| Bounded, plan skipped | Approve short design; record omission conditions. Complete approvals, target choice, actual docs or valid absence, then handoff |
| Bounded, plan required | Approve design/all required plans; approve necessary specs before dependent planning. Prepare target before drafting, complete set before batch/handoff |
| Architectural | Design → written spec → all `writing-plans` plans. Target before drafting; full set before batch/final checks/handoff |
| Non-behavior docs/config | Record scope/criteria/inapplicability. Preserve target/Git/docs-or-absence/handoff |

New planning scope requires list/depth/dependency reassessment and approvals before dependent drafting/commit. Approved-body changes need revised approval except mechanical records below. New implementation scope holds execution until docs/approvals/preparation complete. Running Implementer stops before newly dependent edits; inspect actual changes/Git without retrospective preparation claims. Reflect approved versions through original-commit updates below. Unchanged-document restarts follow handoff lifetime.

contracts.heading: Automatic commit after plan-task acceptance
contracts.text:
## Automatic commit after plan-task acceptance

One approved top-level task is one focused implementation commit. Orchestrator verifies criteria/current checks/findings, accepts by judgment, then immediately commits locally without separate user commit approval. After acceptance, check Git state/scope, stage and commit. Never commit before acceptance or defer until plan completion. Implementer completion is not acceptance; explicit assignment never permits Implementer commits.

Substeps/checkboxes track progress, not commits. Completion marks/reports/passing checks do not establish acceptance; connect conditions/expected results to evidence. Plan omission creates neither new plans nor automatic commits; follow applicable guidance/user requests. Push/merge/publish/deploy/install retain separate approvals. Reviewer timing follows [verification](verification.md#risk-scaled-execution).

1. Before commit verify approved plan version/task ID/accepted scope, actual absolute workspace/repository/branch or detached HEAD/HEAD, staged/unstaged/untracked state and ownership.
2. Verify staged content/paths include only this task and final message. Prove safe separation of other tasks/user changes in shared files. Unrelated staging blocks commit under Preservation rule.
3. After commit verify SHA/message/paths/content, HEAD/branch and remaining state. Successful exit alone proves no completion.
4. Canonically link plan path/version, task ID, acceptance evidence/judgment, required checks/findings, commit results/state, hold/no-change/reuse reasons and remaining final verification.

Hold commits for unmet/unresolved criteria, failed/not-run required checks, undispositioned findings/gaps, scope expansion/revised-plan needs, ownership/staged scope/content mismatch, unexpected workspace/branch/HEAD/Git state or failure/partial completion. Record reason/next action; never waive criteria/checks to commit. Disposition follows Evidence verdict. Inspect actual branch/HEAD/index/working tree/partial completion before retry; uncertain commit creation stops immediate retries. Orchestrator follows [recovery](git-recovery.md), resolves and revalidates evidence.

No-change tasks record acceptance/no change without empty commits. Resume verifies/reuses the same task's SHA/content/validity without duplication. Missing records require actual-result inspection before retry. Normal accepted commits retain valid choice reuse with fresh state/ownership checks. Task acceptance/commit differs from final plan acceptance; remaining QA/Reviewer/integration checks retain their timing.

For final Reviewer findings on committed plan work, define follow-up task/required planning/approvals. Implementer leaves corrections uncommitted through rechecks. Orchestrator refreshes committed state plus uncommitted diff/changed-file list in Reviewer artifacts/briefs. Reuse/assign an independent Reviewer; repeat Implementer → Reviewer without QA reassignment until resolved, then accept and create one focused follow-up commit. Final QA findings retain Implementer → QA before a new commit. Never automatically amend/reset/duplicate originals. Scope expansion retains planning/approval duties.

Local commit authority never permits early planning-document commits. Pre-Implementer approvals/explicit target/batch preparation remain. Never retroactively alter historical spec/plan records. Structural checks prove no live compliance.

Use Conventional Commits `<type>(<scope>): <description>` with concise specific English description, no trailing period, lowercase scope when useful and one logical task. Body/footer only when needed; preserve Git trailers.

contracts.heading: Failure and external-action boundaries
contracts.text: Hold commits for unmet/unresolved criteria, failed/not-run required checks, undispositioned findings/gaps, scope expansion/revised-plan needs, ownership/staged scope/content mismatch, unexpected workspace/branch/HEAD/Git state or failure/partial completion. Record reason/next action; never waive criteria/checks to commit. Disposition follows Evidence verdict. Inspect actual branch/HEAD/index/working tree/partial completion before retry; uncertain commit creation stops immediate retries. Orchestrator follows [recovery](git-recovery.md), resolves and revalidates evidence.

Read this reference
and [handoff preparation](references/handoff-prep.md) before checking

Risk-scaled execution.under the Orchestrator direct path below: under the Orchestrator direct path in [handoff](handoff.md#orchestrator-direct-path-for-small-tasks),
